title.narrative: Enhance the resilience of Tall Refaat, Maskana and AS-Safira communities to winter conditions by restoring access to WASH and Bread basic services (sub-objective 2)

description.narrative: ltpgtltspangtSyria has been amidst a protracted conflict since 2011, leading to extensive damage to critical infrastructure and resulting in widespread poverty, food insecurity and a resurgence of waterborne diseases. The earthquake further aggravated the needs and severely impacted WASH and livelihood infrastructure, challenging people’s access to basic services, particularly water, sewage and bread.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtIn alignment with its strategy and its operational presence in Aleppo governorate, HEKS/EPER seeks to extend further support to vulnerable households in the area through a multi-sectoral, needs-based approach that emphasizes synergies between various sectors and its existing portfolio. The proposed intervention will prioritize the rehabilitation of service delivery infrastructure to promote the resilience of vulnerable underserved communities in hard-to-reach arlt/spangtltspangteas that witness harsh winter weather conditions.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtThrough Field presence and coordination with various stakeholders,11 potential interventions in Tall Refaat and Maskana sub-districts were selected. These interventions were evaluated and prioritized based on several factors, including the severity, the impact of winter conditions, and sustainability. Sustainability here primarily refers to the assurance of electricity or alternative power sources to maintain the functionality of the rehabilitated infrastructures.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtThe project is scheduled to launch in November and wlt/spangtltspangtill span 12 monthsltspangt, with a total cost of $500,000 evenly split between the FAS and WASH sectors. It boasts efficient fund utilization at a rate of less than $6 per beneficiary.lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangt lt/spangtltspangtIn line with the FAS sector objective 3, the WASH sector objective 1, and the HRP objective 3, the proposed interventions seek to achieve several key outcomes:lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangt1-ltspangt Tlt/spangtlt/spangtltspangthe comprehensive rehabilitation of the bakery building in Maskana, including the restoration of one dysfunctional production line. This initiative aims to effectively address sub-optimal access to subsidized bread, which serves as a lifeline for 65,000 residents in the area.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtltspangt2-ltspangt lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/spangtltspangtThe rehabilitation of sewage network in Tall Refaat, with the goal of ensuring equitable access to essential sanitation services for 15,000 individuals as this area has been grappling with sewage water leakage issues, posing a threat to the safety of drinking water and creating an environment conducive to the spread of diseases like Leishmania and other water-borne illnesses.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtltspangt3-ltspangt lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/spangtltspangtThe rehabilitation of a borehole in Sheikh Issa, with the aim of improving access to water for 6,000 individuals who currently have substandard access to potable water, receiving only 10 liters per person per day.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtRecently, due to the hostilities followed by the recent changes in control, Maskana became inaccessible with no clear view on when access will resume. Consequently, after consulting the WASH sector and coordinating with DoWR and HAC, it was found that Abu Sfeita water pumping station is in dire need for rehabilitation. Such intervention will benefit 4,611 individuals, whereby they will have improved access to potable water. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspangtHEKS/EPER will engage qualified contractors, obtaining validation from the Ministry of Water Resources (MoWR)lt/spangtltspangt and the Ministry of Internal Trade and Consumer Protection (MoITCP)ltspangt for the scope of work and technical design. The project primarily centers on community-level technical interventions within public sector infrastructure. HEKS/EPER collaborates with community representatives to ensure their needs and concerns are effectively communicated and addressed, promoting a positive and cooperative approach.lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltspangtFollowing the successful completion of the rehabilitation works, the relevant Ministry will assume responsibility for the continuous operation and maintenance of the rehabilitated infrastructures. This transition to local management not only guarantees long-term sustainability but also leads to improved service delivery to the community.lt/spangtlt/pgt
